title: Nvidia, Oracle, CoreWeave and other AI stocks sink on OpenAI revenue report
source_used: Stocktwits on TradingView and BeInCrypto on Yahoo Finance, both relaying the Financial Times (CNBC original blocked)
key_facts: The Financial Times reported on 8 Oct 2026 that OpenAI told investors its annualised revenue approached about $50 billion at the end of September.
That is roughly $20 billion below the $70 billion figure widely reported late in September, which was based on data first supplied to investors.

The gap comes from different counting: investors tried to match OpenAI to rival Anthropic, which includes sales through cloud partners such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, while OpenAI excludes sales made through third-party cloud channels.
Oracle shares fell more than 5% on 8 Oct, Broadcom nearly 4%, Nvidia more than 2% and Microsoft more than 1% (BeInCrypto on Yahoo Finance).
Two semiconductor funds, SOXX and SMH, fell between 2% and 3%; the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.4% and a gauge of chip companies fell 3.4% (Bloomberg).
OpenAI declined to comment on the disclosures.
quote_evidence: The two AI developers use different accounting methods to calculate annualized performance.
OpenAI declined to comment on the disclosures.
why_it_matters_hint: The share-price drop shows how closely AI stocks track reports of OpenAI sales growth, though the gap is largely about how revenue is counted.
notes: CNBC original blocked (Akamai error page); Quartz and Seeking Alpha also unreadable. Facts come from Stocktwits (TradingView) and the Bloomberg text read for C07-03; the BeInCrypto text read for C07-06 gives the share falls. First reporter is the Financial Times (not read directly).
